name: Project Mogul

summary.text: Project Mogul was an Army Air Forces balloon-borne research project of the late 1940s. The U.S. Air Force's 1995 report 'The Roswell Report: Fact versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert', prepared at the request of Representative Steven Schiff and the General Accounting Office, identified the debris recovered near Roswell in July 1947 as coming from Project Mogul. A 1995 GAO records search found that some Roswell Army Air Field records had been destroyed and that a July 8, 1947 FBI teletype described the recovered object as resembling a weather balloon with a radar reflector. A second Air Force report in 1997, 'Case Closed', attributed reports of bodies to anthropomorphic test dummies dropped from research balloons.

facts.claim: The Air Force's 1995 report, prepared by Colonel Richard L. Weaver and First Lieutenant James McAndrew at the request of Representative Steven Schiff and in support of a GAO records search, identified the debris found on the Foster ranch in 1947 as coming from an Army Air Forces balloon-borne research project code-named MOGUL.
facts.quote: The report identified the debris as coming from an Army Air Forces balloon-borne research project code named MOGUL.

sources.title: 75 Years after the Roswell Incident, What Have We Learned?
The Roswell Report: Fact Versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert

facts.claim: The Air Force completed the first step of its Roswell records effort in July 1994; records describing research under Project Mogul, most of which were never classified, were collected, provided to the GAO and published in one volume.
facts.quote: Records describing research under the MOGUL project, most of which were never classified, were collected, provided to GAO, and published in one volume.

sources.title: 75 Years after the Roswell Incident, What Have We Learned?
The Roswell Report: Fact Versus Fiction in the New Mexico Desert

facts.claim: The GAO's July 28, 1995 report to Representative Schiff (GAO/NSIAD-95-187) found that some Roswell Army Air Field records had been destroyed, with no information on when or under what authority; that under 1947 rules there was no requirement to report the crash of a weather balloon; and that the search yielded two 1947 records, a 509th Bomb Group/RAAF history report and a July 8, 1947 FBI teletype.
facts.quote: some of the records concerning Roswell activities had been destroyed, but there was no information available regarding when or under what authority the records were destroyed

sources.title: Government Records: Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell, New Mexico (GAO/NSIAD-95-187)

facts.claim: The GAO reported that the July 8, 1947 FBI teletype stated the military had reported recovering an object resembling a high-altitude weather balloon with a radar reflector near Roswell, and that other government records reviewed, including previously classified ones, did not mention the crash or recovery of an airborne object near Roswell in July 1947.
facts.quote: The FBI message stated that the military had reported that an object resembling a high-altitude weather balloon with a radar reflector had been recovered near Roswell.

sources.title: Government Records: Results of a Search for Records Concerning the 1947 Crash Near Roswell, New Mexico (GAO/NSIAD-95-187)

facts.claim: The Air Force's 1997 follow-up report 'The Roswell Report: Case Closed', authored by James McAndrew, concluded that reports of bodies at Roswell were attributable to anthropomorphic test dummies dropped from high-altitude research balloons under the unclassified High Dive and Excelsior projects, which it said were widely publicized at the time.
facts.quote: Air Force projects that used anthropomorphic dummies and human subjects were unclassified and widely publicized in newspapers, books, and television.

sources.publisher: Headquarters United States Air Force (via Project Gutenberg)
sources.title: The Roswell Report: Case Closed

facts.claim: Writing in Skeptical Inquirer in 1998, Bernard Gildenberg, a thirty-year veteran of the Holloman Air Force Base Balloon Branch who contributed to the 1997 report, and Dave Thomas said the Roswell story had several sources, including the high-altitude dummy drops and one severe military aircraft accident, and that the report was released in summer 1997 to considerable initial criticism.
facts.quote: the report was released in the summer of 1997 to considerable initial criticism

sources.title: The Air Force's Roswell report: Case Closed (Gildenberg and Thomas)
